summary: The ADR/RFC/governance layer is the strongest anti-certification surface in the repo. Three accepted ADRs — ADR-038 (trust model without a CA), ADR-039 (operator self-publication / machine-verifiable conformance), ADR-040 (federation trust evaluation without certificates) — are the load-bearing "no CA / no operator certification / no human approval" decisions; they deliberately removed the CA-issued certificate and any discretionary human gate, superseding ADR-022 (Certification Level Architecture), ADR-026 (Federation Trust Model) and the CA parts of ADR-027 (root architecture survives). Crucially, M2.19 is MECHANISM-COMPATIBLE with these ADRs (deterministic, evidence-based, no human, no CA, re-derivable, revocable, Rust engines only, Qwen out of the decision path) but conflicts with their absolute TERMINOLOGY: dozens of docs assert "BANZA does not certify" without qualification. The reconciliation M2.19 needs is a precise split between "BANZA does not grant a financial licence / authorise operators / run a CA / make discretionary approvals" (KEEP) versus "BANZA issues a deterministic technical-interoperability certification that a concrete implementation conformed to a public, versioned profile" (NEW). Almost every "não certifica" for BanzAI/Qwen actually SUPPORTS M2.19 (agent does not decide; engines compute) and should be kept; the statements to amend are the entity-level ones ("does not certify operators", governance/engines "não conferem estatuto"). The next free ADR number is ADR-057 (highest existing is ADR-056; no ADR-057 anywhere; no M2.19 references exist yet).

summary: The public website (Next.js app under website/) is built end-to-end on a "conformance = evidence, NOT certification" stance: PASS produces reproducible technical evidence, no one certifies/approves operators, there is no CA, and the honest state today is an empty registry (/operators = [], production_certificates = false). This stance is asserted three ways: (1) user-facing copy on Home, Operadores, Estado, Reference §7 and the footer; (2) the canonical reference markdown content/BANZA_REFERENCIA.md §7 "Conformidade e Evidência" whose report literally states "This report is conformance evidence, not a production certificate."; and (3) a strong lattice of source-level vitest guards that FORBID the words "operador certificado / certificação de operador / certificado de produção / BANZA CA" and require the flow be titled "Conformidade" not "Certificação". M2.19 must introduce a Technical Interoperability Certification that is deterministically derived from the SAME public, revocable, time-bounded evidence the site already surfaces — so it must (a) keep the still-true negations (not a financial licence, no CA, no discretionary approval, no Qwen in the decision path) and (b) rewrite/relax the absolute "não certificação" statements and the tests that ban all certification vocabulary. Terminology is mixed: "certification_level"/"certification_level_achieved" contract fields and the registry "Certificados" counter are already certification-shaped (reusable), while "0 certificados emitidos", "não certificado", "PASS não é certificado", "não certifica" are the obsolete/needs-qualification stance.

summary: The SVG/diagram surface is governed by three documents (docs/reference/BANZA_SVG_REGISTRY.md = the registry; docs/governance/SVG_QUALITY_POLICY.md and docs/governance/SVG_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md = the canonical STYLE/grammar — there is no literal STYLE.md) and two machine guards (tools/check-svg-visual-quality.sh + tools/check-svg-visual-system.sh, plus tools/assert-reference-svgs.sh), all wired via Makefile and .github/workflows/identity-guard.yml. M2.19 must therefore both add new certification-pipeline / certification-lifecycle / responsibility-boundary SVGs and rewrite the guards+policies that would currently reject them, while preserving the still-valid negations (no CA, no financial licence, no discretionary/human approval, no Qwen in the decision path). summary: The banzai surface (banzai-api service + website Workbench components) is built around an absolute "no certification, no CA, no approval" stance enforced at four layers: (1) UI copy constants (banzai-agent.ts FORBIDDEN_PHRASES/AUTHORITY_COPY/BANZAI_AGENT.boundary) plus unit tests that assert those exact strings; (2) deterministic answer ENTRIES in knowledge.js that repeatedly say "não certifica / não há CA nem certificados de operador / PASS é evidência, não certificado"; (3) the Rust routing/boundary layer (route.rs AI-authority detection, boundary.rs BND-OPERATOR-CERTIFICATION category) that refuses "certifica/aprova/licencia operador" and the Qwen SYSTEM_PROMPT rule 2; and (4) a post-response deterministic validator (validate.rs) that hard-BLOCKS any affirmative "issue certificate / certify / certified operator / live certification / BanzAI as certifier" claim. A typed reason_code system already exists (terminal.rs, reasoningTrace.js). For M2.19 the surface must learn to EXPLAIN an engine-determined technical interoperability certification (profile/version/scope/validity/reason-codes/renewal, revocable) while the validator, boundary and prompt continue to forbid BanzAI *granting* it and continue to forbid financial/operator licensing — the hardest tension is validate.rs, which currently blocks the very vocabulary M2.19 introduces.

summary: Every engine under engines/ is a standalone Cargo crate (own Cargo.toml+Cargo.lock, NO workspace) following one pattern: src/lib.rs holds pure, native-testable logic that computes status/reason-codes/SHA-256 hashes IN RUST; src/wasm.rs (feature="wasm" for browser, or #[cfg(target_arch=wasm32)] inline for Node) exposes JSON-in/JSON-out #[wasm_bindgen] fns named <domain>_<verb>_json; each carries BOUNDARY+PROTOCOL_STANCE consts, machine-readable boundary flags, llm_calls=0, external_model_called=false, test_only, fixtures/demo_fixtures, schema()/tool_version(); big json! literals use #![recursion_limit="512"]. contracts/production holds JSON-Schema draft-2020-12 files (*.production.schema.json) with $id under banza.network, _spec_version/_status/_authority/_boundary, additionalProperties:false, and a boundary object of const:true/false flags cross-referenced by absolute $id. The surface is saturated with an OLD ABSOLUTE stance that BANZA "nunca certifica": five engines carry hard deny-lists that FLAG the tokens certificate/certified/certificação/operator certificate/production certificate/operador certificado as violations, protocol-version.json pins production_certificates=false, every production schema asserts not_certificate/not_operator_certificate/certificate_based_trust=false, and the BanzAI decision path (boundary.rs BND-OPERATOR-CERTIFICATION + prompt.rs) refuses "certifica" verbs. All these deny-lists are aimed at OPERATOR (financial) certification but match the bare certification tokens, so M2.19's new Technical Interoperability Certification will trip them unless ADR-057 narrows each list to distinguish technical-interop certification from operator authorisation. There is NO dedicated JSON-Schema CI validator for contracts/production; enforcement rides on per-crate cargo test (rust-engines.yml), the repo-guards gates, and the in-repo schemacheck::validate_against_schema authority in banzai-query-core. A new banza-interoperability-certification crate + two production schemas (Profile + Record) should live in engines/ and contracts/production and CONSUME the existing conformance-evidence, evidence-bundle, operator-manifest, signed-protocol-metadata, revocation and federation-trust-evaluation artifacts plus banza-trust's canonical-JSON/ed25519 sign+verify primitives.

summary: The repo enforces an absolute "no certification" stance across ~90 tools/check-*.sh guards, the Makefile (per-guard `<name>-check:` targets + one giant `.PHONY` line + `pre-commit`), 8 GitHub workflows, Rust engine tests, and website/service test suites. Three enforcement shapes exist: (1) FORBIDDEN/RETIRED token lists that blanket-block "certificação/certification/operador certificado/BANZA CA/certificate authority/production certificate" as ACTIVE copy (svg, public-surface, governance, home, nav, license guards); (2) REQUIRED-negation guards/tests that assert boundary copy like "não certifica"/"PASS não é certificado"/"não é certificação central" and fail if absent; (3) Rust deny-lists + gate tests (banza-reference-trust-model, banza-open-governance, L1–L4/security/m2-gate readiness) that treat any certificate field/flag as INVALID_EVIDENCE and pin `production_certificates(_allowed)=false` / `not_a_certificate=true`. All guards are negation-aware and self-testing; most are wired into `.github/workflows/identity-guard.yml` (45 jobs, push+PR all branches) as thin single-source-of-truth wrappers. M2.19 must NOT simply delete these (the financial-licence / operator-certificate / discretionary-approval / BANZA-CA prohibitions stay); it must NARROW them to permit a new deterministic, engine-determined Technical Interoperability Certification vocabulary while keeping the financial/CA prohibitions, and add a new certification engine + guard + CI step + Makefile/.PHONY registration.
